title: Reader analytics, kept to myself
description: This blog now has real user monitoring: page views, web vitals, errors and which links get clicked, sent to an OpenObserve I run on my own server, only after the reader says yes, and sampled before a byte of the SDK is downloaded. Why a writer wants feedback at all, what the responsible-innovation framework says to leave out, the alternatives I looked at, and the day it produced six measurements of the same files for every one of a reader.

title: Measuring what a coding agent actually costs
description: A self-hosted OpenTelemetry stack for LLM usage, built as an OpenObserve experiment for customers who keep telemetry on prem: two months of getting the numbers wrong, 118,469 spans of which 118 were useful, and what Rosenberg's learning by using says about why the price list told me nothing.

title: Forking Codex to talk to any endpoint
description: How we restored the Chat Completions wire API in a Codex fork, so one coding agent drives local Ollama models, OpenRouter, Azure OpenAI with Entra auth, or any EU-hosted provider. The three patches that made it usable, the branch model that keeps the rebases to an hour, and why Baldwin & Clark's design rules say the interface was the thing to fight for.

title: Exploring LLMs so our customers don't have to
description: Norwegian businesses started asking their consultants this in 2026, after a year of quietly running Claude Code. Two decisions hidden in one question, why the endpoint matters more than the tool, what it actually costs, and what March's explore/exploit dilemma says about how a company ends up on one vendor without ever deciding to.

title: One-click unsubscribe needs a URL per reader and a DKIM tag
description: Three months of running a self-hosted newsletter: double opt-in with no database, why one-click unsubscribe forced me to stop using my mail server's fan-out, and an RFC 8058 DKIM requirement that ends in an anticlimax.
